<reason>B narrowly wins on seasonal shortages: annual crew rehiring undermines A’s principal gradual-adjustment argument, and an uncapped guest-worker program does not establish timely replacement. A landed strong corrections on H-2A law and discrimination enforcement; B also overstated what Arizona and the absence of a numerical forecast prove. Nevertheless, B’s final distinction between readily available evasion and slower lawful recruitment left a consequential shortage risk insufficiently answered under this conjunctive motion.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A exposed B’s incorrect claim that expanding H-2A recruitment requires Congress. B conceded the legal point but preserved the practical objection through processing, housing, and harvest deadlines. That response mattered: removing a numerical cap as an obstacle did not demonstrate that replacement workers would arrive within seasonal hiring windows.</best_rebuttal>
